 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Harish Kumar
 Oral Order

Heard Mr. Kamal Nayan Choubey, learned Senior Advocate along with Mr. Alok Kumar Singh,
learned Advocate for the petitioners.

The State is represented through Mr. Prabhat Ranjan, learned Advocate.
2.

The petitioners are aggrieved with the Memo Patna High Court CWJC No.1470 of 2026(2)
dt.05-02-2026 No.114-2 dated 13.01.2026, issued by the Circle Officer, Madhepura whereby they Purushottam Kumar, vs The State Of Bihar on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5088680/
1 have been directed to remove their houses from the land, in question.

entities.text: Purushottam Kumar, vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The petitioners also sought a declaration that the Acquisition Proceeding initiated vide Memo No. 1580 dated 01.09.2011 has lapsed in terms of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short 'Act, 2013').
3.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Learned Senior Advocate for the petitioners pressing the present application has submitted that the land, in question, was notified to be acquired under Section 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 (in short 'Act, 1894') and the Government takes away the right of the concerned raiyats to file objection under Section 5 (A) of the Act, 1894 in the name of urgency, nonetheless, even after lapse of more than 15 years the petitioners and the subsequent purchasers have neither been given compensation nor the possession has been taken and, as such, the proceeding is deemed to have lapsed in terms of Section 24(2) of the Act, 2013.
4.

It is further contended that identical issue has come up for consideration before a coordinate Bench of this Court in C.W.J.C. No. 10840 of 2025 where the similar notification Patna High Court CWJC No.1470 of 2026(2) dt.05-02-2026 contained in Memo No. 1580 dated 01.09.2011 issued by the Department of Revenue and Land Reforms, Government of Bihar is put to challenge.

entities.text: Department of Revenue and Land Reforms, Government of Bihar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The learned coordinate Bench having taken note of the relevant prescriptions of the Act, 2013, as also the mandate of the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Indore Development Authority Vs. Manoharlal and Others, reported in, (2020) 8 SCC 129 has been pleased to stay the operation of the aforenoted order.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority Vs. Manoharlal and Others, reported in, (2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Despite the aforesaid facts while the petitioners have been continuing on the possession of the land, in question, the Circle Officer, Madhepura has come out with the impugned Memo No.114-2 dated 13.01.2026 by treating the petitioners as encroacher, without following the due procedure.

6. Having considered the submissions advanced by the learned Senior Advocate for the petitioners and taking note of the facts that identical matter has come up for consideration where the operation of the notification contained in Memo No. 1580 dated 01.09.2011 has been stayed, this Court direct the respondent State authorities to ensure filing of the counter affidavit, preferably within a period of four weeks from today.
7. Re-notify this case along with C.W.J.C. No. 10840 of 2025.
Patna High Court CWJC No.1470 of 2026(2) dt.05-02-2026 8.
The impugned Memo No.114-2 dated 13.01.2026 shall remain stayed, so far the petitioners are concerned, till further order.

(Harish Kumar, J) uday/-
